brief: Morgan Stanley's August tally put hyperscaler off-balance-sheet commitments at $3.1 trillion, up from $1.8 trillion in June. After Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and SpaceX filed Q3 10-Qs, a rebuild from primary filings puts disclosed commitments across the hyperscalers, Nvidia, Broadcom and SpaceX at $4.11 trillion, up $992 billion in roughly 90 days. The five Q3 filers alone added $577 billion (23%) quarter over quarter: Meta +$195bn (purchase commitments, data-center leases, residual-value guarantees), Amazon +$131bn, Alphabet +$164bn, Microsoft +$35bn (its purchase-commitment figure is stale, reported only annually), SpaceX +$51bn (+174%, driven by a $40bn GPU lease). Nvidia, Oracle and Broadcom haven't reported Q3 yet, so $4.1 trillion is described as a floor. Goldman's Amanda Lynam separately counts $2.8 trillion across five hyperscalers (an eightfold rise since 2023) and flags inconsistent rating-agency treatment (S&P adjusts for leases, Moody's and Fitch don't) plus companies raising capital preemptively, citing Meta's equity raise. On-balance-sheet debt and leases total only ~$1 trillion, so reported leverage understates the AI complex's obligations more than fourfold. The piece ties this to Alphabet's, and now Amazon's, stock declines and a $1.2 trillion Nasdaq 100 market-cap loss this month.
